title: Price Action Setups
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/0/body: An **inside bar** is a candle whose high and low sit fully **inside the range of the previous candle** (the mother bar). The market is **resting and coiling up**, and a move usually follows out of one side of the mother bar.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/1/body: The common way: trade **with the trend** and enter on a break of the mother bar's high (for a buy), with your stop loss **below the mother bar's low**. Some traders use a tighter stop below the inside bar's own low, but it gets hit more often.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/2/promp: What pattern do the last two candles form?
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/2/expla: The last candle's high and low sit fully inside the big bullish candle before it. That's an inside bar.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/3/promp: Tap the inside bar: the candle whose high and low sit fully inside the previous one.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/3/expla: This candle's high (2390) is below the mother bar's high (2392), and its low (2378) is above the mother's low (2369). The whole candle fits inside the one before.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/4/state: In an inside bar, the second candle's high and low both sit inside the mother bar's range.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/4/expla: That's the definition: its high is lower than (or equal to) the mother's high, and its low is higher than (or equal to) the mother's low. If either one pokes out, it's not an inside bar.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/5/body: An inside bar is more reliable in a **trend** (after a pullback or a strong move) and at **key levels**. Many traders prefer it on higher timeframes like the daily. Back-to-back inside bars in a choppy range are mostly **noise**.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/6/promp: The trend is up. You buy on a break of the mother bar's high, stop loss below its low. Where's take profit at 1:2?
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/7/promp: The trend is up and the last two candles form an inside bar. Where does your buy stop order go? Drag its line.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/7/expla: This setup enters on a break of the mother bar's high. The mother high is 1.0872, so the buy stop sits just above it (say 1.0875). The inside bar's own high (1.0869) is still inside the mother's range, so breaking it confirms nothing.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/8/promp: The trend is up. After a pullback, a strong bullish candle formed, then an inside bar. If it breaks out, which way is more likely?
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/8/expla: An inside bar means compression. In an uptrend, a break above the mother bar is more likely (not certain). Enter on a break of the mother high, stop loss below its low.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/9/sente: In an inside bar setup, the first big candle is the ___ and the small candle inside it is the ___.
lessons/price-action-u2-l1/steps/9/expla: The mother bar sets the range and the inside bar rests within it. A break of the mother bar's range is the entry signal.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/0/body: A **false break** is when price **pushes past** a key level, triggering stop losses and breakout orders, but then **closes back behind the level**. Traders who jumped in on the break get trapped, and their exits can push price the other way.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/1/body: The main sign: the **wick** pokes past the level but the **body closes back inside the range**. A false break candle often looks like a **pin bar**. The faster and sharper the snap back, the stronger the signal.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/2/promp: Tap the candle that made a false break of support.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/2/expla: This candle dipped to 2978 below support but closed above 3,000. Sellers who entered on the break got trapped, and price bounced up.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/3/promp: What does the last candle show?
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/3/expla: The wick went above 1.2700, but the body closed below resistance. The break didn't hold, so it's a false break.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/4/state: To confirm a false break, the candle needs to close back behind the level (inside the range).
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/4/expla: Until the candle closes, you can't tell if the break is real or fake. A close back inside the range means the break was rejected.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/5/title: False break entry and stop loss
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/5/body: Once the false break candle closes, enter **against the break**. Put your **stop loss just past the wick's tip**. The first target is usually **the other side of the range** or the next key level.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/5/tip: If price pushes past the false break's wick again, the setup is invalid. Your stop loss protects you from exactly that.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/6/promp: EUR/USD is ranging between 1.0800 and 1.0900. After a false break below support, you buy. What's the risk-to-reward ratio?
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/7/promp: Price went above resistance but closed back below it (a false break), and you sold at 1.0885. Place your stop loss.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/7/expla: A false break stop loss goes just above the tip of the fake breakout wick, so above 1.0918 (say 1.0925). If price goes past that too, the break was real and the sell idea is dead. Right above resistance (1.0900) is too close; the same kind of swing would stop you out.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/8/promp: Price went above resistance, but the candle closed below the level (a false break). Which way is more likely?
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/8/expla: Buyers who entered on the break are now trapped below the level. A move back down is more likely. Stop loss just above the wick's tip.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/9/promp: Put the steps of a false break setup in order.
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/9/items: Find a key level or range edge
The candle closes back inside the range
Enter against the break, stop loss past the wick
lessons/price-action-u2-l2/steps/9/expla: No level, no false break. Then the push through, then the close back inside to confirm, and finally the entry with a clear stop loss.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/0/body: After a level breaks, price often **comes back to test the broken level** and then keeps going. That return is called a **pullback** or **retest**.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/1/body: A level that used to be **resistance** can become **support** after it breaks (and vice versa). A common explanation: traders who missed the breakout jump in when price returns to the level.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/2/promp: Resistance at 150.00 has broken. What's price's latest move?
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/2/expla: Price closed above 150.00, went higher, and has now come back to test that level without closing below it. That's a pullback.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/3/promp: Tap the candle that broke resistance and closed above it.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/3/expla: The candle before only reached 62,000 with its wick. This is the first candle to close above resistance with a strong body.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/4/state: Every breakout pulls back before the move continues.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/4/expla: Many strong breakouts keep going with no pullback. If your setup is the pullback and none comes, you've missed the trade, and that's better than chasing price.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/5/body: Instead of chasing the breakout candle, wait for price to come back to the level and give a **confirmation signal** (like a pin bar or an engulfing). Your stop loss goes **below the level or below the signal's wick**, and the risk is usually smaller than entering on the breakout candle.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/6/promp: Why do many traders prefer entering on the pullback over chasing the breakout candle?
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/6/optio: A tighter stop loss and a better risk-to-reward
Because entering on the breakout candle is forbidden
Because a pullback trade needs no stop loss
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/6/expla: On a pullback, price is close to the level, so a stop loss behind it is shorter. With the same target, your risk-to-reward gets better.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/7/promp: Gold broke resistance at 2390, came back to it, and formed a bullish pin bar. What's your call?
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/7/expla: The broken resistance is now acting as support, and the bullish pin bar confirms it. Continuation up is more likely. Stop loss below the pin bar's wick.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/8/sente: After a break to the upside, old resistance can act as ___.
lessons/price-action-u2-l3/steps/8/expla: This is called role reversal: an old ceiling can become the new floor after it breaks.
